REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  MARCH 22, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:04 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Nilsen, Brtis, Ciarolla, Robinson

Committee Members Absent:  Griggs, Harik, Zigrang, Martin

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith

DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 22, 2021

MEMBER BRTIS moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO, to:

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE FEBRUARY 22, 2021 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

None.

STAFF ITEMS

  A. COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that COVID case numbers continue to decline. More sectors are opening with
protocols in place. Additionally, there are no changes to the health protocol that would affect the
equestrian community. Staff continues to communicate with the County on changes in holding
horse shows soon. It was discussed by the Committee that Horse Shows are opening in other
parts of the County and staff will research further.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  B. PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER BOARDERS SURVEY

ACM DAVIS provided a brief review of the staff report. CHAIR HUFF asked how the Committee
felt about the survey. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON stated that she thought it was a good
survey. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON added that she noticed that PWEC received high
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  1
MARCH 22, 2021
 scores on customer service, and that there is always room for improvement, but overall, it was
very positive. CHAIR HUFF added that the survey showed that people really like the staff, and it
may be helpful to bring on additional staff to help with the cleaning. GIL HOULE stated that the
information provided from the survey results will help them to evaluate areas of improvement. He
added that they did have some staffing issues during the pandemic but have since hired more
help. CHAIR HUFF suggested in the future PWEC place signage when they are short staffed to
help explain any change in services.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON asked what type of rodent control is used. MR. HOULE
responded that poison is not used. Alternative rodent traps are used where possible. The uptick
in rodents could be attributed to the dry season in the landfill. CHAIR HUFF thanked MR. HOULE.

  C. FOOTING STATUS ON ALL ARENAS (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that staff would like to update the Equestrian Committee on a quarterly basis
for all arena footing and what is being done to maintain the space. Superintendent Goldsmith
stated that over the last thirteen months, the City has implemented a variety of repairs and
maintenance spending $46,000 to date on all repairs and replenishments. He further explained
that sand was added to arenas at Howlett Park and Dapplegray and upgrades were made to the
base of Arenas Three and Four at Howlett Park. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that there has
been additional discussion for upgrades on the dressage arena at Howlett Park which is being
considered. Currently, the City does have a stockpile of GGT and staff budgets for maintenance
material each fiscal year. He concluded that the next project planned is the Chandler Park Arena.

AUDIENCE MEMBER LOUISE KOCH stated that she met with Superintendent Goldsmith and
was grateful for his knowledge. She added that after to speaking to Superintendent Goldsmith
she believes that a sand stockpile to replenish the dressage arena would be a good option.
AUDIENCE MEMBER SCHACHTER stated as a reminder that Chandler Park is in need of repair.

It was noted that Committee Member Griggs who is absent was injured recently in a horse related
accident.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  D. MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that staff is planning the event and is looking at the regular May date. There
may be some modifications in place to meet any County restrictions during the time of the event.
Staff is coordinating with the Mayor to solidify a date and is working to lock in horse rentals for
the event. Due to the current restrictions, staff does not anticipate a scout hosted pancake
breakfast, but is looking at alternative options. Additionally, there is a possibility that the County
will move into the Orange Tier and that transition may loosen more restrictions. CHAIR HUFF
asked if the event is typically held on the first weekend in May. ACM Davis stated that in the past
the Mayor’s Ride was held on the second weekend of May and this year it would fall on May 8,
2021. CHAIR HUFF stated that last year staff discussed hosting the event in the Fall in order to
coordinate with the City Celebration. ACM Davis stated that there is still a possibility to move the
date to a future date in the summer. She added that it was suggested to host the Mayor’s Ride
event closer to the 4th of July holiday last year and asked for suggestions from the Committee as
to a possible date change.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  2
MARCH 22, 2021
 CHAIR HUFF stated that the issue with hosting the event near 4th of July is that most
neighborhoods host their own block parties at that time. She added that the City Celebration date
might work well. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON stated that horses and fireworks do not
work well together and is not in favor of a July 4th date. ACM Davis stated the City Celebration
typically hosts the poker ride in the morning and a Mayor’s ride might conflict with the timing of
that event. COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO asked if it is realistic to plan for the City Celebration
gathering. ACM Davis stated that it is very difficult to say now and explained that staff is looking
to modify most events this year to meet COVID-19 restrictions. CHAIR HUFF added that
vaccinations could have a big impact on the future of group gathering. COMMITTEE MEMBER
BRTIS stated that it is likely in Fall that there will be more precautions taken due to flu season.
ACM Davis thanked the Committee for their feedback and stated that staff will continue to keep
the Committee updated.

  E. WASTE MANAGEMENT MANURE RATE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis provided a brief background of the Waste Management Manure contract. Additionally,
stating that the planned manure rate increase was delayed in 2020 due to the COVID pandemic
and was postponed through June 2021. She continued that after much feedback from the
community the City reformed a Waste Management subcommittee and hired a consultant to help
look at different alternatives to alleviate the large rate increase. ACM Davis provided a
presentation outlining California regulations AB 341, AB 1826 and SB 1383. ACM Davis detailed
what is being proposed to City Council as an amendment to the contract which would introduce
organic waste service and modify rates across all lines of business, considering a more modest
increase to manure rates than originally approved. She explained that with the modification and
added service, residents can expect to see approximately $3.00 a month increase upon the
effective date estimated on July 1, 2021. Additionally, manure rates will increase but not as
significantly as originally approved. ACM Davis added that they worked to negotiate the rate
increases and hope the community sees these options as a viable solution. COMMITTEE
MEMBER ROBINSON stated that she is glad to see that the increase is not as high as initially
proposed. COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN agrees with COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON
and is pleased with the results.

  F. HORSE TRAINER BUSINESS LICENSE LIST (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that staff recently received the latest updated list for registered horse trainers
with the most up to date list totaling nine registered trainers. She explained that typically there
are 21 registered trainers registered but some are still in process. New lists have been posted at
all arenas but will be updated later in the month. ACM Davis added that if anyone is having trouble
registering information or have not received confirmation of your license, to please contact Laurie
in Finance. The City will be scheduling a trainer meeting in April to review the online registration
process and guidelines.

  G. EQUESTRIAN LOG

None to report.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  3
MARCH 22, 2021
 COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A- TRAIL

COMMUNITY MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that there were wet spots on the trail located
behind Ernie Howlett Park tennis courts that may be caused by a neighboring resident and could
be a hazard for riders on the trail. Superintendent Goldsmith stated he would go assess the area.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROBINSON would like to discuss T-shirts for the Committee.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN would like to discuss safety items for the Fourth of July.

ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING 8:03 pm

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

Cynthia Morquecho  __________________________
Community Services Supervisor  Britt Huff, Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  4
MARCH 22, 2021
